To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the metabotropic glutamate‐receptor‐mediated signal‐transduction pathway in cultured C6BU‐ 1 glioma cells resembles NMDA receptor ion‐channel complexes, and this pathway interacts with the 5‐HT receptor signaling pathway.

the metabotropic glutamate (mGlu) receptor in cultured glioma cells has N‐methyl d‐aspartate receptor‐ion channel (NMDA‐R) complex‐like properties, interacts with serotonin 2 (5‐hydroxy tryptamine2) receptor (5‐HT‐2) signaling, and is coupled to phospholipaseC (PLC) via GTP‐binding proteins (G proteins).
the metabotropic glutamate and 5‐HT receptor systems interact in the C6BU‐ 1 glioma cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the pharmacological characterization of metabotropic EAA receptor in C6BU1 glioma cell.
the interaction of metabotropic receptors with 5‐HT receptors and their possible roles in the central nervous system.
the pharmacological properties and signaling of metabotropic glutamate and 5‐HT receptors in C6BU1 glioma cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
glutamate inhibits 5‐HT‐mediated signal‐transduction pathways in C6BU glioma cells by acting at a site on the 5‐HT receptor that is distinct from the binding site of the agonist 5‐HT.
the NMDA‐like glutamate receptor‐ion channel‐coupled phospholipase system is involved in the 5‐HT‐mediated signal pathway in C6BU glioma cells.
the metabotropic glutamate and 5‐HT receptors are closely linked and may have a functional relationship.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the metabotropic EAA receptor has NMDA receptor ion channel complex‐like characteristics in C6BU1 glioma cells, but the inhibitory effect is not a result from the influx of extracellular Ca 2+.
the metabotropic glutamate and 5‐HT receptor systems are coupled to a single GTP‐binding regulatory protein in glioma cells.
in C6BU1 cells, the NMDA‐like metabotropic glutamate and 5‐HT receptor‐stimulated signal transduction pathways are linked to each other.
The main takeaway from our work is that
glutamate receptors in C6BU-1 glioma cells are coupled to pertussi toxin-sensitive G-protein and phospholipases C and that they resemble the NMDAr-ICC.
metabotropic glutamate (mGlu) receptor in glioma cells has NMDA receptor-ion channel complex-like properties and interacts with serotonin 2 receptor-stimulated signal transduction.
the metabotropic glutamate (mGluR) receptor is a member of the NMDA‐type ion channel complex in glioma cells.
